protocol.purpose: Locate whether the fresh original-baseline river regression is specific to E016 or shared with retained E015 under the current run history.
protocol.scope: Diagnostic only. Does not replace, exclude or reclassify any prior timing cohort; no candidate acceptance from this script.
protocol.trigger: E016 primary passed +4.1126% versus E015; fresh original-baseline cohort failed river regression guard in all three pairs, primarily in constructor initialization.
protocol.fixed_inputs: Same frozen complete-cycle evaluator, workload, native binaries, full fixture order, compressed storage, 16 CPU threads and unprofiled environment.
interpretation_rules: Retain all nine runs and all 27 fixture records. Compare full-cycle and component distributions across all arms.
Report original/E015 and original/E016 differences separately from E015/E016; do not infer a unique cause from timing location.
If the regression occurs before graph construction in solve, do not attribute it to graph capture without further evidence.
A favorable diagnostic does not erase the failed cumulative cohort or by itself establish stable cumulative performance.

conclusions: The prior repeatable river regression is not reproduced as a repeatable pattern in this diagnostic. This neither establishes a unique E016 cause nor establishes a shared E015 cause.
River medians: original119.1263, E015116.6824, E016120.6387ms. E016/original median+1.2696%; E015/original-2.0515%; E016/E015+3.3907% but only1/3 block-paired repetitions exceeds3% in each contrast.

All three river init ranges overlap. E016 has higher median init by3.8238ms versus original and3.9109ms versus E015, while median solve is lower by0.7029ms/0.6045ms respectively; component medians are nonadditive. No unique constructor substage or external cause is identified.
Both optimized arms improve flop medians; E016 improves all six block-paired flop solve spans relative to E015. Descriptive arm sums/whole-test evidence remain diagnostic, not new acceptance results.
The failed original-reference E016 cohort remains failed and preserved. No reclassification, exclusion, pooling or replacement with these later measurements.
limits: Three runs per arm, deterministic balanced position order, not randomized or powered significance evidence; predecessor/history/cache/CPU scheduling effects remain possible.
Same-binary timing drift across cohorts is observed, but cause cannot be assigned from it. Do not subtract gains across separately timed cohorts.
Boundary GPU samples show one device/driver,2542MHz SM and45-51C, but do not observe river or constructor internals.
Whole-test includes hashing and scoped destruction; runner process includes output/dashboard/polling. These are not pure end-to-end application metrics.
Original manifest records six source hashes; other candidate source records are additional provenance coverage, not evidence of changes.
next_narrow_evidence_step: Use preserved original/E015/E016 binaries with the existing river-only fixture filter in a predeclared balanced three-arm diagnostic, keeping all repeats and exact states. Compare init and solve separately to assess dependence on the earlier large fixtures. River-only makes river the first process fixture and changes in-process NVRTC/cache history, so it cannot alone isolate allocator versus compiler versus driver causes or overturn the failed full-suite cohort. If init remains ambiguous, instrument constructor substages only in a separate diagnostic derived from the existing D012 approach; keep the frozen evaluator and qualification rule unchanged.
